title: Direct gaps by family
question: Among stable elements and binary compounds with a band gap (Alexandria, PBE), is the share with a direct gap higher for III-V and II-VI compounds than for the rest?

issues.text: 'Good light emitter' is not measured; the direct gap is a proxy for radiative efficiency.
issues.fix: The plan tests the direct gap and names internal quantum efficiency as what it misses (defects, surface recombination).

issues.text: Families are small (a handful of group IV elements), and the sample is limited to cells of up to 4 atoms.
issues.fix: Wilson intervals per family; the contrast pools III-V and II-VI against the rest.

issues.text: Family stands for band structure (ionicity, which band edges sit where), not a cause by itself.
issues.fix: Read it as an association; the diagonal chart shows the mechanism (where the conduction-band minimum is).

alternatives.question: Within II-VI, are the Zn, Cd and Hg chalcogenides (tetrahedral) direct more often than the alkaline-earth ones (rock salt)?
alternatives.why: Drill down: the split was made after looking at the data, so it is a new hypothesis, not a test.

alternatives.question: Within III-V, are the nitrides and arsenides direct and the phosphides of Al and B indirect?
alternatives.why: Drill down: the anion and cation size decide where the conduction band minimum lies.

alternatives.question: Does the direct − fundamental margin shrink as electronegativity difference grows?
alternatives.why: Expand: ionicity as a numeric predictor (delta_chi).

alternatives.question: Do measured gaps confirm the direct/indirect labels?
alternatives.why: Expand: experimental band gaps (e.g. Madelung's Semiconductors: Data Handbook) against PBE.

hypotheses.statement: III-V and II-VI compounds have a direct gap more often than the other materials.
hypotheses.null: The share of direct gaps is the same in III-V and II-VI compounds as in the rest.

concepts.label: Direct band gap
concepts.description: The valence-band top and conduction-band bottom at the same k; here: direct gap − gap ≤ 0.005 eV.

concepts.label: Semiconductor family
concepts.description: Groups of the two elements in a 1:1 compound (III-V, II-VI, ...), from PubChem's electron configurations.

concepts.label: Radiative efficiency
concepts.description: Share of electron-hole recombinations that emit a photon.
concepts.why: What the direct gap stands in for.

strategy.detail: gap_type (direct/indirect); misses defect and surface recombination, which dominate real devices.

data.request: Experimental band gaps and their direct/indirect character for the same compounds
data.source: Madelung, Semiconductors: Data Handbook; NSM Archive (Ioffe Institute)
data.why: PBE underestimates gaps; measured ones would check the labels.

method.summary: Count direct-gap materials per family, divide by the family's materials, compare the shares; a two-proportion z-test for III-V and II-VI against the rest.

steps.title: Sort materials into families
steps.detail: classified: valences of both elements, 1:1 ratio → family.

steps.title: Two-proportion test
steps.detail: ztest and verdict: z and one-sided p.

caveats: PBE band gaps underestimate measured ones by 30–100% (Ge, InAs, InSb come out metallic and are missing here).
Only ground-state structures with up to 4 atoms per cell: wurtzite (4) and zincblende/rocksalt (2) are in, larger cells are not.
A small margin (GaP 0.02 eV) is within the method's error: near-direct materials can flip.
The alkali halides (I-VII) are mostly direct but are insulators (gaps of 4–9 eV): a direct gap in the visible or near infrared is what an LED needs.
Direct gap is necessary for efficient emission, not sufficient: defects and doping decide real devices.
